description_en: According to legend this is one of five stūpas built by Aśoka, the Mauryan king of India, however, there is no evidence that King Aśoka ever visited the Kathmandu Valley. Of the five so-called  Aśoka stupas one is located in the center of Patan and the other four are placed in the cardinal directions of what was the periphery of the ancient city. In Newari the stupas are collectively called Pyãḥthūra and specifically are named Tetāthūra (east), Pūcvathūra (west), Ībahīthūra (north) and Lagãthūra (south). It is quite possible that these stūpas represent some of the oldest structures in the Valley predating the Mauryan Empire.The Aśoka Stūpa South is a grass-covered earthen mound and was originally surrounded by wetlands and ponds (pokharī). Today, most of these water bodies have dried up and a school and an army camp have been built upon its land.DanielWright's History of Nepal (1877, plate x) shows the earliest image of the stupa with plastered shrines facing south and east and a square finial with a pyramid-shaped roof. A wooden frame (symbolising an umbrella) is installed on the roof, likely as part of a week-long tradition that takes place during the onset of the dry season. In another image dated ca.1900, a large gathering of people is seen on top of the Stūpa and a similar wooden frame is visible. The Stūpa has undergone many restorations and embellishments over time. The brick retaining wall that now encircles the Stūpa was built some time before 1967, and a steel balustrade with oil lamps was installed around the perimeter in the 1990s. A brick dome replaced the pyramid roof of the finial and a spire was added to this some time in the middle of the last century.Since 1995, a total of fourdharmadhātumaṇḍalasanddharmadhātujinālayacaityaswere installed around the Stūpa. A new entry gate was added, as were walls, fences and two shrines. The traditional brick path around the Stūpa was covered with stone paving.Gutschow(1997, 86) writes that this southern Stūpa is the largest of the four cardinalstūpasof Lalitpur.Coomaraswamy(1972, 144) states that the four Stūpas of Patan were constructed in an ancient Indian hemispherical style.Legend tells that King Aśoka visited Nepal during the reign of 14th Kiranti King, King Sthaṃko, and commissioned the construction of fivestūpas. It is for this reason that thestūpasare named after Aśoka(Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī19-20).Another legend claims that a merchant named Ratnākara collected "gems from the sea" during the reign of Kind Vīradeva. He became rich and commissioned the fourcaityas (stūpas) on the four sides of Lalitpur in the Kali era 3608-9 on the 5th day of the bright half of Māgha (Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī1956, 71).Aśoka Stūpa South is related to Taṅgaḥ Bāhāḥ (LAL2780) of Patan.The āḥjuluiguritual is usually performed in abāhāḥ, however, in the case of Taṅgaḥ Bāhāḥ the ritual is performed in front of Aśoka Stūpa South (H. VajrācāryaVS 2057, 74). On the full moon day of Asoja, thesaṅghaof the Bāhāḥ offers a wooden umbrella to the Stūpa. The rituals related to this Stūpa are based on Vajrayāna Buddhist traditions. Nowadays, followers of Mahāyāna Buddhism, mostly people from Tibet, also visit the Stūpa. The Aśoka Stūpā Sudhāra Samiti, an organisation founded in 1997, manages the the Stūpa.
description_ne: पाटनको मध्यकालीन नगरक्षेत्र वाहिर चारै दिशामा समान स्वरूपका स्तूपहरू रहेका छन् । यी स्तूपलाई स्थानीय भाषामा प्यंगः थूर (चारवटा थुव) भन्ने चलन छ । पूर्वको तेताथूर (थुव/स्तुप), पश्चिमको पूच्वथूर, उत्तरको ईबहीथूर र दक्षिणमा भएको थूर लगंथूर कहलाउँछ । चारमध्ये लगंथूर आकारमा सबैभन्दा ठुलो छ (Gutschow1997, 86) । इँट, ढुङ्गा वा धातुको आलङ्कारिक प्रयोग नभई सामान्य माटोको ढिस्काका रूपमा हुनु यी चारै स्तूपमा पाइने साझा विशेषता हो (अपवादका रूपमा ईबहीथूरको मौलिक स्वरूप मासी पुनःनिर्माण भैसकेको छ) । चैत्य वास्तुको विकास प्रारम्भमा यस्तै माटोको ढिस्को निर्माणबाट भएको थियो । कुमारस्वामीले यी चार स्तूपको मूल स्वरूप जस्ताको तस्तै हालसम्म रहिरहेको भन्दै यिनिहरू प्राचीन भारतीय ढिस्को वास्तु शैली अनुरूप बनाइएको कुरा उल्लेख गरेका छन् (Coomaraswamy1972, 144) । यी स्तूपको ऐतिहासिकतबारे विभिन्न विद्वानहरूबाट अड्कलबाजी भए तापनि ती अनुमानलाई सिद्ध गर्ने पुरातात्विक प्रमाणको अभाव देखिन्छ ।यी स्तूपहरू राजा अशोकले बनाएका हुन् भन्ने विश्वास पाटनवासीमा पाइन्छ ।नेपालिकभूपवंशावली(19-20) मा पनि किराती राजा स्थुंकोको पालामा अशोक नेपाल आउँदा उनले ठाउँ-ठाउँमा चैत्य निर्माण गरेको कुरा उल्लेख छ । देवमाला वंशावलीमा राजा वीरदेवको पालामा रत्नाकर नामक व्यापारीले धन कमाएर ल्याई ललितपुरको चार दिशामा कलिगत ३६०८-९ मा चार चैत्य बनाएको कुरा उल्लेख छ । वंशावली र लोकोक्ति जस्ता कमजोर आधार बाहेक यिनको प्राचीनतालाई निरूपण गर्ने अभिलिखित प्रमाण पाइएको छैन ।सामान्य माटोको ढिस्काको रूपमा रहेको स्तूपमा अन्य धार्मिक वस्तु थप्दै जाने तथा साज-सज्जामा जोड दिइएको पाइँदैन । राइटद्वारा प्रकाशित पुस्तकमा (1877, plate x) यस स्तूपको चित्रमा चौतर्फी ध्यानी बुद्धका गवाक्ष र माथि पिरामिड आकारको संरचना देख्न सकिन्छ । सन् १९०० को दशकतिर खिचिएको फोटोमा स्तूपको ढिस्कोलाई घेरिएको पर्खाल नभएबाट उक्त पर्खालको निर्माण पनि सो समयपछि मात्र बनाइएको थाहा हुन्छ । सन् १९९५ पछि भने स्तूपका साथै यसको आसपास विविध धार्मिक वस्तु तथा साज-सज्जाका सामग्री थपिँदै लगिएको छ । नयाँ संरचनाहरू थपिँदै जादाँ स्तूपको मौलिकपन लोप भएको अवस्था छ ।Pruscha(1975, 131) ले स्पूपको शिरोभागमा भएको चैत्य र चारदिशाका ध्यानीबुद्ध गवाक्ष सन् १८९८ मा निर्माण गरिएको भनेका छन् । उक्त अवसरमा आयोजित भोजमा राजा सुरेन्द्र पनि आमन्त्रित थिए । त्यसै गरीPruscha(1975, 131) ले स्तूपमा सन् १८८१, १८९९ र १९२७ मा पनि पूजा सम्पन्न गरिएको कुरा उल्लेख गरेका छन् तर त्यसको कुनै स्रोत भने दिएका छैनन् ।यस स्तूपको सम्बन्ध पाटनको तंगःबाहाःसंग छ। बाहाः-बहीमा संघका जेष्ठ सदस्यहरूलाई आ:जु लुइगु संस्कार गरिन्छ । पाटनको तंगः बाहाः (LAL2780) संघमा भने उक्त संस्कार बाहाःमा नभई यस स्तूपको सामुन्ने गर्ने परम्परा छ (H. Vajrācārya, VS 2057, 74) । सोही संघबाट यस स्तूपमा असोज पूर्णिमाका दिन काष्ठछत्र चढाउने परम्परा छ ।  पहिला शहर बाहिर एकान्त ठाउँमा रहेको स्तूप समयक्रममा व्यस्त सहर माझ पर्न गएको छ । पाटनको बज्रयानी परम्परामा आधारित पूजा-पाठ हुने यस स्तूपमा तिब्बती (महायानी) बौद्ध अनुयायीहरूको पनि चहल-पहल बढ्न थालेको छ । यस स्तूपको व्यवस्थापनका लागि सन् १९९७ मा 'अशोक स्तूपा सुधार समिति' नामक संस्था गठन भएको थियो र सो समितिले सक्रिय भूमिका निर्वाह गरिरहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Buddha statues were fixed on top of the Stūpa
historical_events.event_description: According toPruscha(1975, 131), these four cardinal Buddha statues were consecrated in 1878 CE with a religious feast attended by King Surendra Śāha. Pruscha does provide any references for his knowledge of this event.
This is the oldestdharmadhātu maṇḍalaof the surrounding monuments; it was commissioned by Mañjuvajra and his family in 1881 CE.
Pruscha(1975, 131) mentions that a worship was organised in the Stūpa in 1881, though he does not mention any sources.
Pruscha(1975, 131) mentions that a worship took place in the Stupa in 1899, though he does not mention any sources.
Pruscha(1975, 131) makes mention of a worship organised in the Stūpa in 1927, though he does not mention any sources.
Acaityawas constructed in front of the Stūpa.
Adharmadhātujinālaya caityawas commissioned by Mānavīra, Mānakāji, Śrīmāyā and other family members.
Adharmadhātujinālaya caityawas commissioned by Buddha Ratna Mānandhara from Vijeśvarī, Kathmandu.
Adharmadhātujinālaya caityawas commissioned by Bābukāji Maharjana, Aṣṭalakṣmī and other members of their family.
Adharmadhātujinālaya caityawas commissioned by Sidulāla Maharjan and his wife Kayo.
Herākājī Śākya constructed adharmadhātujinālaya caityain commemoration of the late Vajrarāja Śākya.
A bell was offered to Akṣobhya by Candra Bhāi Śākya from Okubāhāḥ, Patan

Two stone lions flank the modern gate of the Caitya. Gaṇeśarāja, his wife Indirā and some of their other family members commissioned the construction of these lion statues in memory of their parents Keśavarāja (Pvāḥ Syāḥ) and Surjamāyā Tāmrākāra.
Hirāmāyā and other family members commissioned adharmadhātu maṇḍalain memory of Bābukājī Maharjana.
Nāmasaṅgīti Khalaḥ of Lagankhel commissioned this Phalcā and had the Vairocana Statue placed inside it.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the main entrance, addition of praying wheels, addition of agilt pinnacle, minor renovations
historical_events.event_description: Aśoka Stupā Sudhāra Samiti commissioned minor renovations of the Stūpa. An entrance gate was made on the bank of the main road and a garden was constructed to the east of the Stūpa. Prayer wheels were added to the surroundingdharmadhātujinālaya caitya. Bābujāji Śākya also offered a golden pinnacle with a parasol, which was placed on top of the Stūpa.
Thedharmadhātu maṇḍalawas commissioned by Bābukājī, his wife Cirimāyā Maharjana and other members of their family.
Hirāmāyā Maharjana and other members of his family commissioned adharmadhātujinālaya caityain memory of Bābukāji Maharjana and Hirāmāyā Maharjana.
Anāma Khaḍkā commissioned adharmadhātujinālaya caityain memory of Topabahādura Khaḍkā, Yadukumārī Khaḍkā and Gaurī Khaḍkā.
Kājilāla Avāle from Bhindyalāchi Patanand his wife Jñānīmāyā Avāle commissioned adharmadhātujinālaya caitya.
Only the date is inscribed on thedharmadhātujinālaya caitya.
Only the date is inscribed on thedharmadhātujinālaya caitya.
A damaged inscription can be found to the north of the Stūpa. It is not clear what the inscription commemorates; only the date remains legible.
Kānchī Avāle and other members of their family commissioned thedharmadhātujinālaya caityain memory of Rāmalāla Avāle and Keśarī Avāle.
